previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right scapular pain, dyspnea, and fever, initially concerning for pneumonia or pulmonary embolism. Imaging showed no evidence of PE or acute fracture, and chest X-ray findings were stable. A urinary tract infection caused by E. coli was identified, and treatment with Bactrim was initiated. Her musculoskeletal chest pain improved with analgesics, and gastrointestinal symptoms resolved during the stay. She was evaluated for possible gastric ulcer, prompting outpatient endoscopy referral. The patient was discharged home on antibiotics, with instructions to monitor weight and follow up for INR checks and GI evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ woman with a past medical history 
significant for HIV and recurrent UTIs/cystitis who presents to 
the ED because her UCx from ___ grew out E. coli. She reported 
no urinary symptoms and has a chronic Foley in place. In the ED, 
she was given IV Zosyn x1. Because she was asymptomatic, her UCx 
likely reflected that she is a chronic colonizer as opposed to 
truly infected. Treatment was not continued. Also, she has a 
history of chronic cellulitis. She reported 1 week of worsening 
edema. On physical examination, her LLE was erythematous and 
warm to touch. Her laboratory values were unremarkable. After 
touching base with her PCP, her presentation was felt to be 
consistent with her known cellulitis, and treatment was not 
started. She was advised to remain in the hospital for further 
evaluation and management. Although she understood our concerns 
and the risks of leaving, she chose to leave against medical 
advice.
